newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates dip as reserves stocked up.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates dip as reserves stocked up.

text.p: German call money rates began the week on a slightly softer note after banks' reserve holdings at the Bundesbank climbed late last week, easing pressures seen on Friday to stock up those reserves.
"Call money rates were tighter Friday as people scrambled to stock up the reserves but due to that effort the numbers looked better on Monday, easing the pressure a little bit," one dealer said.
Overnight rates traded between 3.05/10 percent on Monday commpared with Friday's 3.10/25 percent rates.

In light of current liquidity conditions, dealers predicted more sideways trading this week, adding they expected the Bundesbank to keep the money market rate fixed at this week's policy-setting council meeting on Thursday.

Banks' reserves at the Bundesbank rose to 40.3 billion marks on Friday from 39.1 billion marks on Thursday. Meanwhile the monthly average rate climbed to 39.8 billion marks compared with 39.6 billion marks. Lombard borrowings totalled 500 million marks on Friday. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.15775 percent on Monday compared with 3.15067 percent on Friday.
